data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"A test constrains its subject when the test is installed before the subject can mutate, and the mutation is shown to fail first; otherwise, the test describes the subject because the mutation has already been accepted by the time the test runs; the 1-of-9 and 3-of-26 distributions arise because compile.py's shown-to-fail-first installation gives the registry authority that ordinary guards lack.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the test is run before the mutation is installed, the test constrains the mutation by rejecting it.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the registry is not part of the installation, the shown-to-fail-first step does not constrain the subject.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the mutation affects a module that is not ordinarily guarded, the distribution may differ.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"The temporal ordering of installation and testing determines whether the test acts as a filter or a mirror. When the mutation is planted before the test, the test only describes what the mutation already did.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
